readability.where: This page's main text in your website editor.
readability.when: After any confirmed access problems; review one important page at a time.
steps: Open this page in the website editor. Find its main paragraphs, not the navigation or footer.
Read the paragraphs aloud. Find a sentence that is hard to follow; the current audit may not identify the exact sentence for you.
If it helps, divide that sentence into two shorter sentences or replace an unfamiliar phrase with a clear one. Keep the original meaning, important facts, and necessary detail.
Preview and publish the change. Ask someone unfamiliar with the subject to read it.
readability.verify: Check that the published paragraph is accurate and easier to understand. A readability number is only a review cue, not proof of quality or AI citations.
readability.caution: Do not rewrite a privacy policy, terms, or other legal wording without the appropriate review.

comprehensiveness.owner: Content editor and someone who knows the subject
comprehensiveness.where: The main content of this specific page.
comprehensiveness.when: After checking important technical issues; start with pages customers use to make decisions.
steps: Write down what a visitor came to this page to do or learn.
Read the page and note any essential question a visitor would reasonably expect it to answer.
If something important is missing, edit the page and add a short, accurate answer or a link to a relevant existing page. Use facts your business can verify.
Preview and publish. Check that the added information helps the visitor complete the page's purpose.
comprehensiveness.verify: Have a knowledgeable person check that the key questions are answered accurately.
comprehensiveness.caution: A low word count does not prove content is weak. Do not pad contact, utility, privacy, or legal pages to raise a score.

flow.where: The paragraphs in this page's main content.
flow.when: During the next editorial review, after more important issues.
steps: Open the page editor and read the main paragraphs in order.
If the subject changes abruptly, move related paragraphs together or add a short sentence that explains the connection.
Remove any added transition that sounds forced or repeats information, then preview and publish.
flow.verify: Ask a reader whether the explanation is easy to follow from one idea to the next.
flow.caution: A transition-word count does not prove that a page has poor flow. Do not add phrases just to satisfy a score.

lsi_keywords.where: The page and a separately collected set of real customer questions.
lsi_keywords.when: Only as an optional manual review; this audit did not measure related-topic coverage.
steps: List genuine questions your intended readers ask about this page's subject.
Compare those questions with the information actually on the page.
Add or link to an accurate answer only when it is useful and appropriate to the page.
lsi_keywords.verify: Ask a subject-matter expert to review the answers. This is not an automated keyword-gap or ranking test.
lsi_keywords.caution: The audit did not measure a semantic or competitor gap.

answer_completeness.where: A relevant question or explanatory section on this page.
answer_completeness.when: When updating content on an important customer-facing page.
steps: Choose a real question that visitors ask and that fits this page's purpose.
In the page editor, place the question in a meaningful heading and answer it directly underneath using accurate, specific information.
Include the essential context a reader needs; link to a supporting page if more detail would help.
Preview and publish the answer after the business owner or subject expert approves it.
answer_completeness.verify: Read the answer without the rest of the page. Check that it is accurate, understandable, and actually answers the question.
answer_completeness.caution: There is no proven universal answer length. Do not add an FAQ to a page where it does not belong.

factual_density.where: Claims, numbers, and examples in this page's main text.
factual_density.when: During content review; prioritize claims customers use to make decisions.
steps: Read the page and identify a factual claim or statistic that would benefit from support.
Find a reliable original source, or confirm the fact with the person responsible for it. Check the date and whether it applies to the claim.
Edit the sentence to match the evidence and link to the source when appropriate. Remove or qualify a claim you cannot support.
Preview and publish only after the facts have been approved.
factual_density.verify: Follow the source link and confirm it supports the published statement.
factual_density.caution: Do not invent statistics or add numbers solely to improve a score. Some pages need no statistics.

citability.where: Promotional or factual claims in this page's text.
citability.when: During the next review of customer-facing copy.
steps: Open the page and look for claims such as 'best', 'guaranteed', or other statements that promise a result.
Confirm whether each claim is supportable. Replace an unsupported claim with a specific, accurate description of what the business actually offers.
Keep genuine calls to action and the business's voice; the aim is accuracy and clarity, not removing all marketing.
Have the business owner approve the wording before publishing.
citability.verify: A reviewer can explain or substantiate the published claims.
citability.caution: A promotional-word count is a heuristic. Neutral wording does not guarantee AI citations.

structure.owner: Website editor; ask a developer if headings are controlled by a template
structure.where: The headings on this page, in the page editor or page template.
structure.when: Review important shared templates and customer-facing pages first.
steps: Open the page in your website editor and identify its main title and section headings. If needed, a developer can inspect the page's heading tags.
Make sure the main title describes the page. Use Heading 2 for main sections and Heading 3 for subsections when that reflects the actual content.
Use the editor's heading-level control rather than simply making text larger. Keep the current visual design where possible.
Preview the page, check that headings describe the sections in a sensible order, and publish.
structure.verify: Inspect the published heading outline or ask a developer to check it. This audit may not say which individual heading needs changing.
structure.caution: Do not add or change headings mechanically just to raise a score; use a structure that makes sense for the page.

ai_optimization.where: An appropriate service, product, or educational section on this page.
ai_optimization.when: During content improvements for important pages.
steps: Choose a real question that customers ask and that belongs on this page.
In the page editor, add the question as a clear heading and write an accurate answer directly underneath.
Include relevant details your business can verify and link to a related page if it helps the reader.
Preview, get the answer approved, and publish.
ai_optimization.verify: Ask a reader whether the question is answered clearly without needing to search elsewhere on the page.
ai_optimization.caution: A page does not need a FAQ just for a score. Avoid adding one to legal, privacy, or utility pages unless it genuinely belongs.

image_alt.where: The image settings for this page's images.
image_alt.when: When the audit identifies images to review; begin with images that convey information.
steps: Open this page in the website editor and inspect its images and their alternative-text settings.
For each meaningful image, write a short description of the information it conveys in this page's context.
For an image that is purely decorative, an empty alt value can be appropriate; ask a developer if the editor does not offer that choice.
Save and publish, then inspect the image properties or ask an accessibility reviewer to check them.
image_alt.verify: Meaningful images have useful descriptions, decorative images do not create unnecessary announcements, and the page still looks correct.
image_alt.caution: The audit may only detect the presence of an alt attribute, not whether its wording is helpful.

platform_specificity.where: A separately configured AI-answer monitoring process, not this page's HTML alone.
platform_specificity.when: Optional; this audit did not run live platform tests.
steps: Choose a small set of real customer questions and the AI products you are authorized to test.
Run the same questions consistently and record the platform, date, response, and any cited URLs.
Repeat later under comparable conditions and review the results as a limited sample.
platform_specificity.verify: Confirm each recorded citation against the actual response. Results can vary and are not a guarantee.
platform_specificity.caution: This audit did not measure live AI answers, rankings, or citations.

content_type.where: Sections of this page that explain items, steps, or comparisons.
content_type.when: When revising the page for clarity.
steps: Read the page and identify information that is genuinely a sequence, a set of items, or a comparison.
In the page editor, use a numbered list for real steps, a bulleted list for related items, or a table for a comparison when it makes the information easier to use.
Keep the underlying facts accurate and preview the layout on a phone before publishing.
content_type.verify: The format helps a visitor understand the information and works on small screens.
content_type.caution: Do not add a list or table solely to satisfy a check.

semantic_clarity.where: The main paragraphs on this page.
steps: Read the page and look for long sentences or words such as 'it' and 'they' whose meaning is unclear.
Name the person, product, or topic directly where doing so removes ambiguity.
Split a difficult sentence only if the meaning stays accurate. Preview and publish the approved text.
semantic_clarity.verify: Ask someone unfamiliar with the page to explain the sentence back to you.
semantic_clarity.caution: A sentence-length heuristic does not establish voice, meaning, or AI performance.

ai_bot_access.owner: Website developer or technical SEO specialist, with the site owner's approval
ai_bot_access.where: The site's robots.txt and the affected page path.
ai_bot_access.when: Before content work if an intended search crawler is actually blocked.
steps: Open the site's robots.txt file and find the rule that applies to the named crawler and this page's path.
Decide with the owner whether that specific crawler should access that specific public page. Search crawlers and training crawlers can serve different purposes.
If the block is unintended, have the developer adjust only the relevant rule, keeping private and sensitive paths protected.
Publish robots.txt and test the affected path against the intended crawler's rules.
ai_bot_access.verify: The intended public path has the intended rule, and private paths remain protected.
ai_bot_access.caution: Never replace the whole robots.txt file or allow every bot blindly. Robots rules are not access control for private information.

schema_validator.owner: Website developer or person managing structured data; the owner confirms business facts
schema_validator.where: The existing structured-data code for this page or the site's schema/SEO settings.
schema_validator.when: Review after confirming whether the page's existing markup is missing, invalid, or simply not observed.
steps: Open the page source or your schema settings and look for existing structured data, especially a script marked application/ld+json. The audit may not identify the exact error or code location.
Test the full page URL or complete code with the Schema Markup Validator at https://validator.schema.org/; note the specific error and affected object.

If code is invalid, correct that existing code. If appropriate markup is genuinely absent, choose a type that describes the actual page and use only accurate information visible to visitors. Do not add duplicate business objects.
Save a backup, make the change in the correct page template or SEO settings, and test the complete code again before publishing.
After publishing, test the live URL. For Google-supported rich-result types, also use https://search.google.com/test/rich-results.
schema_validator.verify: The intended page's complete markup parses and the relevant validator reports no errors for the object you changed. A test result is not a promise of a rich result or AI citation.
schema_validator.caution: Valid JSON alone does not establish correct schema or truthful content. Some markup may be rendered by JavaScript, which this audit did not inspect.

sitemap_depth.owner: Website developer or person managing the site's SEO settings
sitemap_depth.where: The website's XML sitemap and the page's canonical URL.
sitemap_depth.when: After confirming the page should be public and indexed.
steps: Confirm that this page is meant to be public and identify its preferred, canonical URL.
Find the site's sitemap, often linked from robots.txt or generated by the website platform; do not assume its address.
If the correct public URL is genuinely absent, use the platform's sitemap settings or ask the developer to add it. Do not add private or duplicate URLs.
Publish the sitemap and open it to confirm the URL is present. Submit or inspect it in the verified Google Search Console property if available.
sitemap_depth.verify: The current sitemap contains the intended canonical URL. Sitemap inclusion alone does not prove indexing.
sitemap_depth.caution: A limited or failed sitemap fetch cannot prove that a URL is absent.

page_speed.where: This page's initial HTML and, separately, a performance testing tool.
page_speed.when: Before content work if essential page content is not available in the HTML returned to crawlers.
steps: Open the live page and note a short piece of its important visible text.
View the page source and search for that text. If it is absent, ask the developer whether important content is inserted only after JavaScript runs.
If appropriate, have the developer provide the important content in the initial HTML or another supported rendering approach, then test again.
To assess loading speed, run a separate PageSpeed Insights or comparable performance test; this audit's HTML check is not a speed test.
page_speed.verify: The relevant content is available to the intended crawler, and any separate performance result is reviewed on its own terms.
page_speed.caution: Do not assume a page is slow or blank for users just because initial HTML was limited.

freshness.where: An article or other page where an update date helps visitors.
freshness.when: When a substantive update is actually made.
steps: Decide whether an update date is relevant for this type of page; many utility and evergreen pages do not need one.
Review the content and make any necessary factual or substantive corrections.
Use the website's article settings or an appropriate date element to display the true revision date.
Preview and publish, checking that any structured-data date matches the real update.
freshness.verify: The date is visible or properly declared where appropriate and reflects a genuine revision.
freshness.caution: Do not change dates without substantive updates simply to raise a score.

citations.where: Specific claims on this page that need supporting evidence.
citations.when: When reviewing factual claims on important content pages.
steps: Find a claim or statistic that needs support; not every page needs an external citation.
Find the original, relevant source and check that it actually supports the claim and is current enough for the context.
In the page editor, link the supporting phrase or name the source next to the claim. Correct or remove the claim if it cannot be supported.
Publish and test the link.
citations.verify: A reader can follow the link to evidence that supports the specific claim.
citations.caution: An external link count does not prove authority, factual accuracy, or AI citations.

eeat_signals.where: Author or business details on relevant articles and business pages.
eeat_signals.when: During content review where authorship or business identity helps the reader.
steps: Identify who is genuinely responsible for the article or page: a real person or the organization.
Add an accurate byline or business description where useful. For an article, link to a real author or organization page if one exists.
Include only qualifications and responsibilities the business can verify. Preview and publish after approval.
eeat_signals.verify: The published attribution matches the responsible person or organization and its information is truthful.
eeat_signals.caution: Do not invent credentials or add a personal author to every page just for a score.

knowledge_graph.owner: Website developer; the business owner confirms official profiles
knowledge_graph.where: The existing Organization or business structured-data object, where relevant.
knowledge_graph.when: After confirming the real official profiles and locating the current schema.
steps: Ask the business owner which external profiles genuinely belong to the business. Do not guess or create profiles for a score.
Find the existing Organization, LocalBusiness, or other appropriate business object in the site's structured-data settings or application/ld+json code.
Add the verified profile URLs to that object's sameAs array, using correct JSON punctuation. Edit the existing object rather than adding a duplicate.
Test the complete code with https://validator.schema.org/, publish the change, and test the intended live page.
knowledge_graph.verify: The intended business object contains only verified profile URLs and the complete markup validates.
knowledge_graph.caution: sameAs is not universally required on every page. A page count does not prove that 25 separate edits are needed.

topical_authority.where: Relevant sentences in this page's main text.
topical_authority.when: While updating useful content and related pages.
steps: Identify one or two genuinely related pages on your own website that would help a reader of this page.
In the page editor, link a descriptive phrase to the relevant existing page. For example, use the page topic rather than 'click here'.
Preview and publish, then follow each new link to confirm it works.
topical_authority.verify: Each link leads to the correct public page and is useful in context.
topical_authority.caution: A link count alone does not establish topical authority. Do not add unnecessary links for a score.
